sentence: This project studies why gene therapy for the bleeding disorder hemophilia has not stayed stable, so a safe and lasting cure can be found.
This project tests computer methods that help deep learning models give more reliable results across patient subgroups when diagnosing and treating pulmonary tuberculosis and sepsis.
This project tests whether teaching socioscientific reasoning skills alongside a gene editing curriculum supplement and laboratory experiences changes how people engage with science.
This project gives statistical and bioinformatic help to HIV research, including study design and database design.
This project builds machine learning models that use large clinical datasets to spot hospitalized patients likely to deteriorate and the reasons why.
This project sets up a genetics research center on inflammatory bowel disease that draws on genetics, immunology and technologies.
This project makes and studies anti-glycan antibodies as a possible alternative to antibiotics for Staphylococcus aureus infections.
This project studies how to diagnose, treat and prevent hearing loss, tinnitus and balance problems.
This project tests whether antibodies that block interferon-beta can help T cell therapies work better against HIV.
This project studies how non-coding genetic variants change a type of immune cell and the risk of arthritis.
This project tests small molecular compounds that improve protein quality so blood stem cells keep working after growing in culture for gene therapy.
This project builds nanoparticles made of elastin-like polypeptide to deliver gene replacement and genome-editing therapies for cystic fibrosis.
This project screens protein sequences in mammals to find tags that carry molecules between connected neurons without harmful viruses.
This project studies how physical function and geriatric assessment relate to treatment outcomes in older adults with colorectal cancer.
This project studies how mutant bone marrow cells make thyroid cancer resist common treatments and how to overcome that resistance.
This project studies how adipose tissue and gene expression in the breast tumor microenvironment relate to breast cancer outcomes.
This project studies how circulating tumor cells in hepatoblastoma resist chemotherapy and spread, aiming to develop targeted therapies.
This project studies how proteins are sorted to the correct compartments that release neurotransmitters in the nervous system.
This project studies how immigration status relates to use of sexual and reproductive healthcare among Asian immigrant women.
